Nos ha encantado el alojamiento de Antonio.
Cuando llegamos nos estaba esperando Antonio, el propietario, que fue encantador con toda la familia, y al poco tiempo llegó Paula que nos enseñó la casa y nos facilitó un plano de la ciudad y nos hizo recomendaciones sobre los sitios que debíamos visitar así como sobre los mejores lugares para comer e ir de compras, transporte, etc, y tras ello tuvo el detalle de acercarnos al centro de Oporto en su propio coche (gracias Paula). 
En cuanto al alojamiento, está muy bien y es tal como aparece en las fotos.
Es una vivienda situada el el Foz de Oporto, muy cerca de la rivera del Duero, y a 10 minutos del centro en coche. Cerca de la casa hay varias paradas de bus y una de tranvía, además hay algunas tiendas y cafeterías, y relativamente cerca hay varios supermercados (Lidl, Continente...)
La casa se encuentra en una calle vecinal donde se aparca fácilmente y de forma segura.
La vivienda está recién reformada con muy buen gusto, consta de una estancia principal con salón y cocina tipo office bien equipada (incluso había alimentos para el desayuno), en la parte de salón hay un sofá cama, una habitación principal con cama de matrimonio, aseo con ducha y un pequeño cuarto con un espejo perchero donde dejar las maletas o el carrito del niño. La casa está fenomenal y es perfecta para pasar unos días en Oporto.

Como puntos a tener en cuenta:

-Casa en muy buen estado. 
-Buena situación. 
-Transporte público cercano. 
-Flexibilidad en las horas de llegada y salida.
-Casero muy atento.
-Facilidad de aparcamiento.

En definitiva, el alojamiento es 100% recomendable, y cuando regresemos a Oporto repetiremos seguro.

Which leads us to the next issue – stray cat feces and stains on the steps. It was cleaned now and then, but not nearly often enough.

The building is old and full of ‘old house noises’, from neighbors and the environment. While some of this can be charming, I would have expected other things to be in order, easy things like tightening a door bolt so that it doesn’t rattle whenever someone downstairs breathes.

All in all we’re happy enough considering how cheap the place is and its great location, but there are things we want people to know about before deciding whether to rent.

This is the most beautiful place I've stayed on AirBnb. It's set back in a quiet part of the island, a short walk from the water and parks, and has a beautiful garden with fruit trees and a wide porch on the ground floor. A perfect spot to just relax and listen to the birds and complete privacy from the street. The view of the sea from the living room on the top floor is amazing. I have used Airbnb in four different countries, and Sanem´s place was my best experience ever. The spatial arrangement of the house, which I speculate would have been built in the 50s or 60s, is great: two bedrooms are in the first floor, luminous but protected from direct exposure to sunlight, excellent for peaceful sleep. A spacious and nicely decorated living room upstairs boasts a commanding view of the garden, the sea, and the neighboring island (Heybeliada). The living room connects to a kitchen and a balcony overlooking the garden where we enjoyed our meals. The garden was my favorite spot. It is not for those who love neatly arranged, engineered, and regularly maintained gardens. Sanem´s is an essentially picturesque garden with wild plants that look like being there for ages. There are regularized pockets where Sanem has planted tomatoes, cucumbers, and green peppers. I loved watering them. She graciously let us taste mulberries and plums. Four different plum trees, two different mulberry trees, a cherry tree, a sour cherry tree, fig tree, vines, roses, loquat, and of course the sublime pine tree partly covered by a delightful bougainvillea... Yes, this is still considered to be Istanbul. The notorious phaeton noises and manure smells of Büyükada stay away from this house. We only smelt flowers and post-rain soil, and heard beautiful seagulls whose concert sabotaged occasionally by gangs of crows plotting to take plums and mulberries away... Despite all its peacefulness, the house is not completely isolated: there are two small groceries and a restaurant just about fifty meters down the street. Sanem is a lovely person. She met us at the check-in, made sure we had a pleasant stay, and encouraged us to contact her anytime should there be any inconvenience, which never happened. Great house, dream garden.

We were staying at another house, which was bigger and cheaper, but due to volcanic activity we were evacuated from that house. The Airbnb agent contacted us and helped find for us a place, but since it was already 7 pm, we didn't have much choice so he found us this place that was posted to be good for 8 people. I didn't know it was only a 2 bedroom house so I said ok we will take it. Contacted the host and she said the house was not ready, but for us she would try to clean it up fast, which we really appreciate it. When we came they were waiting for us while finishing drying the towels for us. The House is located in a beautiful dead end with jungle trees around it, but at night its all dark, not a single light on a street. The House has 2 bedrooms and a very small living room, when the sofa bed is folded out there is almost no room to pass. Would not recommend sleeping on the sofa, its old, uncomfortable and stinky. For this  reason I would only recommend groups up to 6 people to get this place, the dining table would maximum accommodate only for 6 people also. So this place would be great for up to 6 people, but for 8 people it was a nightmare... There were some bugs coming trough the door net, so do not keep the door open, the net doesn't shut tightly leaving  gaps for bugs. We accidently broke the glass from the top of a small coffee table, we were honest about it and told them about it and included 40$ that we left for the replacement of the glass which seems reasonable. Later I was contacted and said the replacement would cost around 120$,  they were very rude about it, called me names, and when I offered them to pay them their asking amount they were just continue being negative and ignored me. Would I go again to this place? not really after my experience with it, especially there are better choices around.

neighborhood_overview: While our mailing address is Captain Cook, our home is actually located in a rural setting within the village of Kealia, which is the center of a large cattle ranch.  There is nothing between us and the ocean but the ranch land comprised mostly of  tropical forest.  While we have neighbors on both sides, Hale Honu is very private with many plantings and trees on the property lines.  We are mid-way between Hookena Beach State Park to the south, and Place of Refuge National Historic Park to the north, which is adjacent to "Two Step," one of the best snorkeling locations on the Big Island.  The Hookena Beach bay area is also the play ground and resting place for a pod of dolphins that are often seen during early mornings or evenings. It is a ten minute drive to either of these locations, and a short walk to a small convenience store in the central village.  We are 70 miles from Volcano National Park - a 90 minute drive of spectacular scenery.
notes: There is a land telephone line available for local use and toll-free numbers but calling cards are needed to place long distance calls.  The quality of cell phone access depends on the provider.  We use Verizon but that service is often not as firm as we would like.  Our Wi-Fi service is through Hawaiian Telcom.
transit: Hale Honu is 20 miles south of Kailua-Kona and 27 miles from the Kona International Airport.  A rental car is essential.
access: A key to the front door is located in a coded lock box adjacent to the front door. This is a fully functioning home located on a half acre of tropical garden including fruit trees (papaya, mango, avocado and tangerine when in season). Pine-apples are also available for guests to harvest when ripe.
interaction: Bob and Nancy live in Arvada, CO, but our Hawaii next door neighbors, Gina and Abby, serve as caretakers of the property.  Gina is also the house keeper and landscaper and will be available during your visit to answer questions or help with any problems that might arise.
house_rules: Hale Honu is a smoke-free home.  We ask that guests needing to smoke do so outside.

This is an excellent place. Very private. Loved seeing the pigs and cattle in the field and listening to the coqui frogs that serenaded us each night. The ocean view is amazing and the lanai was perfect for relaxing after a day of exploring.  Will definitely stay there again.

The place is very secluded from the usual touristy Kona Coast. With that you definitely will drive more to get to anything, but it’s convenient to the south end of the island. The coqui frogs definitely are something you’ll adjust to liking, but be aware it’s definitely noticeable at night (the frogs). If your looking for a large cottage like house near Captain Cook, look no further, plenty of room and plenty of nature.

Hale Hona was like home away from home. It has everything you need to enjoy and explore the island. We really enjoyed the lanai for meals and outdoor time at the house. The beds were very comfortable and the kitchen was well equipped for all our cooking needs. 
The house is located outside the busyness of Kona but close enough for an easy drive to the shops there and that much closer to the south to the beaches and volcano park. There are also a number of beaches close by, each unique in its own way. Two step beach has amazing snorkelling that we wish we had discovered the first day so we could have gone back every day of our trip. 
We had a great stay and wish we could have stayed longer.

Robert is a nice host. However, you have to be aware that many, many lizards live in the house. You have to be ok with cohabitating with them and all that it entails (general cleanliness is affected, especially with carpeting).
Such a cute place in an awesome location. The geckos are so fun and the town is delightful
Awesome

We loved how it was away from the tourist areas but we were still so close to everything. Robert was super helpful and gave us thoughts of ideas to do and fun things to explore with the kids. As well as where to shop. Very helpful since we’ve never been here before. We loved the home, it felt homie & the geckos were super fun to watch!!!! Thank you!

Hale Honu was the perfect vacation home for us.  It was very spacious and well equipped for meals and day tripping. Very convenient to many good swimming and snorkelling beaches and villages for local shopping.  It was away from the touristy part of Kona and felt very relaxing.  It was special having that great view from the lanai every day, reminding us of the paradise we were visiting.  Robert and Nancy's remarks and guidance were spot on and very helpful.  We did not have one incident with the house in our 2 week visit.  Thanks so much the our hosts for making our visit so fantastic and memorable!

Hale Honu was perfect for our stay on the Kailua-Kona side of the island. We greatly appreciated the fully stocked kitchen (particularly the coffee grinder for our Kona Joe’s coffee), snorkel/beach gear, laundry, and local recommendations, and the location was close to all the best snorkeling on the island!  I wasn’t stoked about the gecko that dropped on my head during breakfast on the lanai, but the rest of my group was extremely entertained. Robert was super quick to respond to any questions we had (which were few because he provided us with all the info we could possibly need beforehand), and I even got a sweet Christmas card and Hawaii calendar prior to our trip!   Highly recommend!

Solo hay que contar qu ela casa tiene muchas cosas antigua y no es moderna pero esta muy limpia. Volveremos.
